title: TypeScript SDK: Unified streaming consumer playbook & migration guide
creator: Ava Thompson
description: Create a pragmatic playbook, example gallery, and lightweight helper utilities to unify how consumers use streaming responses from the TypeScript SDK across two dominant primitives: AsyncIterator (for-await-of) and Web ReadableStream (Web Streams). This ticket bundles API ergonomics (auto-detection, simple adapters), migration recipes for existing users, and tests + examples demonstrating cancellation, backpressure, and resumability.
background: We have multiple internal and customer-reported patterns for consuming streaming LLM responses: direct AsyncIterator (Node for-await-of), Web Streams (browser ReadableStream), and custom ad-hoc adapters. This causes confusion: inconsistent cancellation semantics, tricky backpressure handling, and repeated example code in docs. Prior tickets addressed pieces of this (adapters, retry surface), but there is no single source-of-truth guidance or small helper library surface to make migration easy and safe.
goals: 1) Provide ergonomic API surface on the SDK that returns both primitives or a thin dual-consumer wrapper. 2) Offer conversion helpers: toAsyncIterable(), toWebStream(), fromWebStream(). 3) Document migration steps with code examples for common usage patterns (simple display streaming, chunked processing, latency-sensitive UI, resilient reconnects). 4) Add tests and examples that cover cancellation, backpressure, and resumable token playback.
non_goals: 1) Major runtime rearchitecture. 2) Creating a full-featured stream processing library (we'll keep helpers minimal). 3) Server-side protocol changes.
proposal: Expose a small, documented helper module (exports: streamToAsyncIterable, asyncIterableToWebStream, createStreamConsumer) and extend the SDK response object with opt-in dualStream() that returns a stable wrapper with the following guarantees: - deterministic cancellation via AbortSignal - consistent backpressure semantics (pull-based) where possible - idempotent close/cleanup - hooks for automatic retry/resume (best-effort using last-token checkpointing provided by server where available). For browser builds, prefer ReadableStream. For Node/CLI, prefer AsyncIterable by default. Provide explicit factory options to override.
api_surface:
- SDK response: response.stream() -> AsyncIterable<string | Uint8Array> (backwards-compatible)
- SDK response: response.webStream() -> ReadableStream<string | Uint8Array> (browser-first)
- helpers: streamToAsyncIterable(readableStream, options), asyncIterableToWebStream(asyncIterable, options), createConsumingLoop(streamLike, {signal, onChunk, onError, onDone})
acceptance_criteria: 1) Library helpers implemented and exported in SDK package. 2) Minimal docs page with 6 runnable examples (Node for-await-of, Browser ReadableStream, cancellation, backpressure queueing, resumable reconnect, retry-on-transient-error). 3) Unit and integration tests covering cancel semantics, double-close safety, and basic backpressure behavior. 4) Migration guide PR merged into docs site. 5) Performance benchmark that shows helper overhead <3% on median latency for typical 2-8 token chunk sizes.
examples_highlights: 1) Simple UI stream (browser): use webStream(), TextDecoderStream, and element.append. 2) Server-side pipeline: asyncIterable -> TransformStream -> batch encoder -> logger. 3) Cancel on navigation: show abort controller wiring across routers. 4) Resumable consumption: checkpoint last token id and request resume token from server on reconnect. 5) Retry transient errors with exponential backoff and idempotent chunk replay.
testing_plan: - Unit tests for helpers converting between primitives. - Simulated network interruption tests: inject mid-stream error and assert resume path or proper error propagation. - Backpressure tests using a slow consumer to ensure SDK does not buffer unboundedly. - Browser-headless integration tests to validate ReadableStream flow and pipeTo usage. - Load test showing <3% overhead on typical workloads.
rollout_plan: 1) Implement helpers behind a feature-flag in SDK canary release. 2) Publish examples and doc drafts. 3) Collect internal feedback from DX + Solutions Engineers for 1 week. 4) Promote to stable in sdk-2.8.0 if no regressions and docs are approved. 5) Notify customers via changelog + migration guide.
risks_and_mitigation: - Risk: subtle cancellation mismatches between Node streams and Web Streams. Mitigation: canonical mapping layer that translates AbortSignal -> reader.cancel()/iterator.return(). - Risk: helper introduces measurable overhead. Mitigation: keep adapters zero-copy where possible and benchmark early; allow consumers to bypass helpers to access raw reader/iterator. - Risk: resume semantics are best-effort due to server constraints. Mitigation: document caveats; only enable automatic resume when server sends stable checkpoint tokens.
notes: Prefer minimal, well-documented helpers rather than a large streaming SDK surface.
Align naming with existing SDK APIs: stream(), webStream(), dualStream(). Avoid ambiguous names like 'bridge' in public docs.
Coordinate with docs engineers for runnable sandbox examples (StackBlitz for browser flows, Node examples in repo).
Discuss with TS SDK maintainers to ensure no conflicts with existing stream-related PRs (see related_issues).
updates: 2026-02-16: Spike complete — implemented two prototype adapters (node->web, web->node) and perf smoke test. Node prototype uses async generator delegating to ReadableStreamDefaultReader.read().

2026-02-22: Decision: Export explicit helper functions instead of automatically returning dual primitives from every endpoint to avoid surface bloat. We'll add response.dualStream() as opt-in factory.
2026-03-02: Added AbortSignal-first cancellation convention. Tests added to assert that controller.abort() triggers iterator.return() and reader.cancel().
2026-03-08: UX review with Developer Experience — suggested additional example demonstrating file streaming to disk with proper backpressure handling. Added to acceptance criteria.
2026-03-10: Began drafting docs PR. Running browser-headless tests locally. Can move to in-review once CI fixes flakiness in pipeTo test.
